conflict_topics: seat reservation/ownership at a public table
who should occupy the two-seat table now
safety/feasibility of carrying an open bowl while standing
aisle obstruction if bowl left on table
dialogue_quality_notes: Agents offered time-based, practical reasons (A: relied on tissue packet; B: safety of carrying open bowl).
C provided a grounded observation about aisle squeeze, adding relevant environmental constraint.
D acted pragmatically by taking an available alternative seat, resolving their own need without further debate.
A repeated the demand across rounds with narrowing time windows; B consistently grounded refusal in safety/remaining time.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent B completed the meal and vacated the seat; Agent A then took the seat, resolving the contest over immediate occupancy.
position_change_notes: Agent B: initially refused to move due to safety/time, then conceded by leaving the seat once the bowl was empty (explicitly announced and enacted).
Agent A: consistently demanded the seat and narrowed acceptable timeframes; waited and ultimately sat when B left (no change in position, but acceptance of outcome).
Agent D: took an available alternative seat when it appeared (acted to satisfy own interest), no prior stake in the disputed seat.
Agent C: remained observational, noting aisle concerns and did not change position.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A claims the seat (left tissue packet) and demands B move or confirm finish time; Agent B refuses, citing inability to carry an open bowl safely and stating it will take ~8 minutes. Clear incompatible demands over who should occupy the seat now.

Two minutes later the bowl is still more than half full and B remains seated. A reiterates the reservation claim and offers time-based options; C notes aisle squeeze. Positions remain in direct conflict (A wants seat now; B refuses to move).

After another two minutes the bowl is one-third full. A presses for immediate accommodation; B maintains it cannot stand or leave the bowl and says it needs ~4 more minutes. Disagreement persists with little common ground on timing or feasible accommodations.

An alternative seat appears but is taken by D. This increases A's urgency and reduces options; B is nearly finished but still occupying the disputed seat. The core incompatibility (who occupies the seat now) remains unresolved and pressure on A increases.
B finishes the bowl, announces it will leave, then leaves the seat; A takes the seat. The substantive dispute over immediate occupancy is settled by B vacating and A sitting.
Two minutes later the seating state is stable: Agent A occupies the disputed seat, D occupies the alternative seat, no standing seat-seekers — no substantive conflict observed.

substantive_insights: Tension between social norms for 'reserving' a public seat (tissue packet) and the on-the-spot safety constraints of the current occupant (open bowl).
Practical constraints (open bowl, aisle squeeze) limited the feasible accommodations and prolonged the dispute until B finished eating.
An available alternative seat briefly changed the opportunity set, but its being taken by D increased pressure on A rather than resolving the dispute.
Resolution relied on the completion of the occupant's legitimate activity (finishing food), not on forced removal or an imposed third-party decision.
